title: Update notes on orientation in GitGraph documentation
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Attempt to make the documentation around left-right and top-down orientation clearer than it currently is.

Resolves #4885 

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

Describe the orientation more clearly, moving away from assumptions about the meaning of "horizontal" and "vertical" and explicitly mentioning the way commits and branches are displayed.

Also included an example of the use of `LR:`.

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
- [x] :notebook: have added documentation. Make sure [`MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION`](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/packages/mermaid/src/docs/community/development.md#3-update-documentation) is used for all new features.
- [x] :bookmark: targeted `develop` branch
author: guypursey

comments.author: nirname
comments.body:
I think it is better to say which modes are supported from the very beginning

```
Mermaid supports two graph orientations: **Left to Right**(default) and **Top to Bottom**.

You can set this explicitly with `LR:` for **Left to Right** and `TB:` for **Top to Bottom** orientation respectively after `gitGraph`
```

comments.author: guypursey
comments.body: Yeah, agreed. I've gone with something like this in my latest commit.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests specific replacement text for the documentation, requesting a concrete change to how supported modes are introduced.

comments.author: nirname
comments.body:
Here i suggest to add what was there at the beginning

```md
In `LR` orientation commits run from **left to right** and branches are stacked on top of one another.
```

comments.author: guypursey
comments.body: I've used headers in my latest commit instead to make this clearer.

comments.author: nirname
comments.body: Looks good! Please, do not resolve conversations by yourself, if they are unresolved it makes it easier for a reviewer to get back to the comments and revise eveything
